title: Oura Announces IPO Targeting $2.2B
subtitle: The Finnish health-tracking ring manufacturer is going public
excerpt: Oura, the Finnish health-tracking ring company, has filed for an initial public offering aiming to raise up to $2.2 billion with 50 million shares.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Oura, the Finnish manufacturer of the health-monitoring ring, initiated an initial public offering (IPO) process this Monday, seeking to raise up to $2.2 billion through the sale of 50 million shares.

Initial Public Offering Details

The share price is set between $40 and $44, totaling a potential fundraising of $2.2 billion at the upper limit. The operation represents the company's largest fundraising attempt to date.

Recent Financial Performance

In the nine-month period ending June 30, Oura posted revenue of $1.2 billion, up from $697 million in the same period the previous year. The net result was negative, with a loss of $924 million.

Sales and User Base

During the same interval, the company sold 4.1 million rings, up from 1.8 million units sold the previous year. The subscription service, which costs $5.99 per month, had 5 million paid members as of June 2026, with 72% being women and 27% over the age of 45.

Positioning in the Wearables Market

Oura competes with brands like Fitbit and the Apple Watch, but differentiates itself by offering a screenless device, similar to the Whoop tracker, focused on users who prefer fewer interruptions. Other manufacturers, such as Samsung, have also launched products in the smart ring category.

Features Offered by the Oura Ring

The ring captures sleep, activity, readiness, stress, heart health, metabolic health, and women's health data, making the information available through a dedicated app. The absence of a screen allows the device to operate for about a week on a single charge.

With information from Yahoo Finance.
